transcript.content: Hello, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I hope it’s all right to say it this way, Doctor. I’ve been having a little trouble at church. I don’t mean to make a scene, but sometimes I do odd things, I guess. Like I’ll stand by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and just not move for a while… or I’ll keep folding the same stack of napkins over and over even when folks are waiting on me. It’s embarrassing, and I thought maybe I should come talk to someone.

When you're standing there holding the spoon or folding the napkins repeatedly, are you aware of what's happening and able to stop if you try, or does it feel like your body just won't move or respond?

I’m… I’m aware enough, I think. I know folks are there and I know I’m supposed to be serving or helping. It’s just like I get stuck doing the wrong thing — holding that spoon up or folding those napkins again and again — and I don’t stop right away, even when people are waiting. I don’t mean to be difficult, Doctor. It just looks odd, I know.

When you get stuck holding the spoon or folding the napkins, does it feel like you're following an urge or thought that pushes you to keep doing it, or does it feel more like your body just becomes stiff and unresponsive on its own?

I’m not sure it’s an urge, exactly, Doctor. I don’t have some big thought telling me to do it. It’s more that I’m just there by the potluck table and… I keep holding the spoon up, or I keep folding those same napkins, even though people are waiting. I know it must look strange. I’m sorry if that doesn’t answer it quite right.

Aside from these episodes of getting stuck, have you noticed anything unusual lately, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that others find strange or hard to believe?

No… I don’t think so, Doctor. I mean, I haven’t noticed anything like voices, not like that. And I don’t think I have any strange beliefs. I mostly just feel embarrassed about getting stuck at church. Is that… is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or new medications, or do you use alcohol or any drugs, around the time these episodes started?

I… I don’t think there’s anything like that, Doctor. No big illness or bump on the head that I can think of. I’m not using drugs or anything. I don’t believe there’s been anything new around when it started… unless I’m forgetting something small. Is that the kind of answer you need?

Aside from these episodes, have you noticed any changes in your emotions or how you interact with others—like feeling less interested in talking with people, showing less expression, or pulling away from friends and family over the past few months?

I don’t think so, Doctor… not that I’ve noticed. I still talk to people when I’m there, and I don’t mean to pull away. Maybe I’m a little quieter because I feel embarrassed, but I don’t think my feelings have changed much. Is that alright to say?
Do you have any ongoing medical conditions—like thyroid problems, diabetes, seizures, or other neurological issues—that a doctor has diagnosed or treated you for in the past?

Not that I know of, Doctor. I don’t think anyone has told me I have those kinds of problems… thyroid or sugar or seizures. I’ve been pretty fortunate, I suppose. If there’s something specific you want me to remember, I can try.
Have you or anyone around you noticed any shaking, muscle stiffness, unusual movements, or things like fever or excessive sweating around the time these episodes happen?

No, I don’t think so, Doctor. I haven’t noticed shaking or stiffness, and I don’t think I’ve had a fever or been sweating like that when it happens. At least, nobody’s told me they saw anything unusual. Is that helpful?
Have you had any recent blood tests, brain scans, or other medical work-ups done to check for possible physical causes of these episodes?

I don’t think I’ve had anything like that done recently, Doctor… not scans or special tests. Maybe just the usual things if they took them, but I’m not sure. No one told me there was some physical cause. Is that okay?
Have you or any close family members ever been diagnosed with a mental illness, such as schizophrenia or another psychotic disorder, in the past?

I’m not really sure, Doctor. I don’t know of anyone in my close family being told they had something like that. People didn’t talk much about those things when I was younger, you know… but as far as I know, no. Is that the kind of answer you mean?
During these episodes when you get stuck, do you ever feel confused about where you are or what's happening around you, or are you always fully alert and clear-headed?

I’m not sure, Doctor… I don’t think I feel confused exactly. It’s more like I just get stuck, and afterward I can’t always explain it well. I think I know where I am, most of the time. I hope that makes sense.

Before these episodes at church started, had you ever gone through a period where you felt suspicious of others, heard things that weren't there, or had beliefs that others told you didn't make sense?

No, I don’t think so, Doctor… not before the church thing started. I mean, I may have worried about people now and then like anybody does, but I don’t remember hearing things or having strange beliefs people told me were wrong. At least, not that I can think of. Is that alright?
Can you tell me approximately when these episodes of getting stuck first began, and whether they came on suddenly over a day or two, or gradually developed over weeks or months?

I think it’s been… maybe around six months, Doctor. It didn’t feel like it happened all at once in a day or two. More like little by little people started noticing I’d get stuck or my talking wasn’t always easy to follow. I didn’t mean for it to come out that way. Is that helpful?

You mentioned that lately your talking hasn't always been easy to follow - can you tell me more about that? Do you notice your thoughts jumping between unrelated topics, or others telling you that your sentences don't quite make sense?

Well… yes, a little, I suppose. I don’t mean to do it. Like when the ladies at church ask me about the blankets, or choir practice, I try to answer plain, but then my words sort of wander off. I’ll start on one thing and then be talking about beans, or hymns, or my roses, and I can see folks looking at me like they can’t quite find what I’m saying.

It’s not all the time, Doctor. I do try to make sense. But sometimes it comes out crooked, I guess. Is that what you mean?
Over these past six months, have you noticed any change in your ability to take care of daily things—like cooking, cleaning, or managing your usual responsibilities—compared to before this started?

Well… I still do most things at home, I think. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I have had to step back some at church… choir and the little volunteering things. I started mixing up plans, or who was supposed to do what, and then someone would have to fix it after me. I could tell people were getting a little uncomfortable, so I thought it was better if I didn’t handle as much.

I hope that answers what you’re asking, Doctor.
I’m sorry, Doctor… I think I may have missed the question just then. Could you say that last part again? I want to answer it right for you.
Over these past six months, have you or your family noticed any new problems with your memory, like forgetting names, getting confused about dates, or losing track of familiar routines?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed anything like that, Doctor… not in any big way. I mean, I’m older, so sometimes a name takes a minute to come to me, but I wouldn’t want to make that into something it isn’t.

My family hasn’t said much about me forgetting dates or not knowing my routines. I still know my usual day well enough, I think. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over these past six months, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss, ongoing fatigue, weakness, or other physical changes in your body that you haven't mentioned yet?

No, Doctor… I don’t think so. My weight seems about the same to me, and I haven’t noticed any new weakness or anything like that.

I do get tired sometimes, but I think that’s just… normal for my age, maybe. Nothing that I’d know to call a big change. Is that okay—does that answer it?
Have you ever had any episodes of losing consciousness, staring spells, or seizures—times when you blacked out or didn't remember what happened for a few moments?

No, Doctor… I don’t think I’ve had anything like that. I haven’t blacked out or had anyone tell me I was staring off and not responding.

Sometimes I might get a little distracted, but not losing time like that. I hope that’s what you mean.

No, I can’t think of any times like that. I haven’t had spells where I passed out or woke up not knowing what happened.

I mean, I can get quiet or lost in thought sometimes, but I don’t think it’s anything like a seizure or blackout. Is that all right?
